subject.title: [Architecture] Migration of transient plugin state to Agent-Scoped SQLite cache tables

question: Should external plugins receive agent-scoped host storage, and if so, what trusted principal may select the agent identity and what lifecycle and quota rules apply?
rationale: Current main intentionally limits host-managed keyed storage to bundled or trusted official plugins, while the proposal would broaden that privilege and bind persisted data to agent identity; maintainer intent is required to define that product and security policy.

options.title: Extend keyed store narrowly
options.body: Add optional host-derived agent scoping to the existing keyed-store API after specifying trust, quotas, cleanup, and isolation tests.

options.title: Resolve trust only
options.body: Address the external-plugin entitlement problem tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/92516 while retaining plugin-scoped shared storage.

options.title: Keep external ownership
options.body: Require ordinary external plugins to own their persistence and reserve host SQLite stores for bundled or trusted official plugins.

recommendation.title: Extend keyed store narrowly
recommendation.body: Add optional host-derived agent scoping to the existing keyed-store API after specifying trust, quotas, cleanup, and isolation tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing keyed-store feature and its semantics are directly connected to amknight's prior work.
